    Task: The first snow falls in hushed, crisp whispers,  
    A silent hymn to winter’s quiet reign.  
    The world is wrapped in gray, a hush so still,  
    As if the earth itself has paused to lean.  

    Trees wear diamonds, ground is dressed in white,  
    Each flake a star that dances, then takes flight.  
    The air grows thin, a breath of frozen grace,  
    While shadows stretch in twilight’s soft embrace.  

    Children laugh, their breath a ghostly trail,  
    And roads are silvered, as if dreams are made.  
    The snow, a veil that veils the old, the worn,  
    And whispers of the coming, cold, soft dawn.  

    Oh, first snow—your hush, your hushed, sweet song,  
    A blanket for the heart, a hush for the wrong.  
    You turn the world to something pure and new,  
    A quiet beginning, as the north winds blow.
